chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Back at Minton's, then Ella Fitzgerald's band at the Cocoanut Grove
summary: After leaving Louis around October 1941 he returned to Minton's, then went to Boston with Eddie Barefield and Dizzy to join Ella's band, replacing Bill Beason.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, all right, let's go back. So you went to Penn Station and picked up your drums.
Yeah.
(Laughter)
And then what happened?
Well, okay. I came back straight to Minton's.
Oh, yeah.
And left my drums.
Yeah.
And I went back to work at Minton's.
Yeah.
Now, this was about '41. So I left Louis, it was still -- well, it was warm down south. It must have been in autumn.
Yeah.
You know, it must have been around October.
Yeah.

Then I came back to Minton's and finished the winter out there. And then Diz and I -- this was in 1942, now. This was in '40 also, because Diz was married in -- no, '41, that's right. So we went to Boston with Ella. It was Eddie Bearfield.
Yeah, just shortly after Chick died.
Who asked me would I be interested in joining the band.
Yeah.
And I said, "Well, yeah." He said, "Well, we're getting Diz." I said, "Oh, beautiful." So we went to Boston, at the Cocoanut Grove, you know, the place that burned and killed all those people?
Yeah.
Well, that's where we were working.
How about that. They played Boston before, at Lavoggi's (PHONETIC).
Oh, did they?
Yeah. While Chick was still alive.
Yeah. Well, we played the Cocoanut Grove and then we went to New Haven and played a theater on Sunday.
Yeah.
I think every Sunday they played this theater in New Haven.
Oh, I see. Yeah.
And I remember Diz had just written that thing he did for Woody Herman. "Down Under," they called it. It was in a film or something.
: Oh.
And then --
Yeah.
: Chick died in June, 1940.
Yeah, right. It was early 1941 we went, because I took Bill Beeson's place.
Oh, I was just trying to remember who (Unintelligible) was playing drums with [her in the beginning.]
It was Bill Beeson, Beverly Peer and Tommy Fulford.
: That's right.
And I joined the band. We went --
: Was Tim Gale the road manager?
Right. He was, because I had a hassle with him about some drums.
: He wasn't nearly as bad as Mo.
